events.title: Trinity's capture turns into a massacre
events.summary: Four cops breach Room 303 of the fire-gutted Heart O' The City Hotel and take Trinity at gunpoint; she submits slowly, hands behind her head. Outside, Agent Smith corrects the Lieutenant's belief that the raid is succeeding, telling him his two units are already dead. Back in the room, the moment the Big Cop reaches with the cuffs, Trinity moves: she breaks the arrest and kills the squad in a blur of inhuman speed, leaving herself the only one standing as a flashlight rocks to stillness.
events.action: The raid that looked like a clean collar is revealed to have been a trap closing on the cops, not on her.

state_triples.reading: Her compliance was never defeat but a calculation — she buys the seconds she needs and lets them mistake her stillness for helplessness. The cuff reaching for her is the line she drew: the first touch becomes the last thing any of them controls, and the violence that follows runs on a clock only she can read. The single dropped 'Shit' is the only crack in a composure that never actually broke, and its meaning — relief, irritation, or something colder — stays hers alone.

state_triples.reading: Smith exists in this beat to puncture the ordinary world's illusion of control. affects_outside.enables: The police operation at the hotel is wiped out, leaving the field clear for the Agents to take over the pursuit of Trinity themselves — and confirming to them that the target is far beyond ordinary law enforcement.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: The Lieutenant's claim to be handling 'one little girl' is exposed as a fatal miscalculation, costing him his men and his control of the case; the ordinary police can no longer pretend this is a containment they can manage.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Whoever is feeding Trinity her instructions — and whoever sent the Agents — now knows the police line has been broken and the operation has escalated beyond a simple raid; both sides have been told, in blood and in cold correction, that the rules have changed.

events.title: Trinity's escape across the rooftops to the phone
events.summary: Informed that her hotel hardline is dead and that Agents are on site, Trinity drops the phone and runs for a separate pay phone at Wells and Lake. She slips past Agent Brown's unit in the hall onto the fire escape, is forced upward when Agent Smith blocks the alley, and crosses the rooftops with impossible grace while the cops fall behind and Brown matches her leap. She dives through a window into a back stairwell, crashes down injured but still moving, finds no pursuer behind her, then races a garbage truck to a ringing phone and answers it a split-second before the truck destroys the booth, leaving no body.

state_triples.reading: Trinity moves through this whole run as a soldier converting panic into procedure: the deep breath Morpheus demands in the hotel is the same self-regulation she holds on the rooftop, where calm is not the absence of fear but a decision not to let it touch her hands or her stride. What the arc reveals is that her discipline is exactly what the Agents can match and therefore cannot stop — she escapes not by being faster than Brown but by committing to an exit his power over physics has no answer for

Morpheus is the event's still point: he absorbs Trinity's fear and hands back a single concrete instruction, and his refusal to panic on the line is the discipline that lets her re-collect herself and run. The arc only shows him at its opening, but his voice is the thread the whole escape hangs on — the same calm, directive authority the scene layer notes will later shepherd Neo, so his role here is to establish the guide whose composure becomes the crew's way out.

state_triples.reading: Jones is the collective's clean voice: he names Trinity's escape without flinching and confirms the search is 'already begun' before Smith even orders it, showing the apparatus executing itself. The scene layer reads his flat delivery as the absence of private stake — the quiet satisfaction of a system working exactly as designed — and his 'it's already begun' is the event's closing note of a machine that has already turned its gaze toward the next target.

The Agents function as one jurisdiction rather than three people: they absorb the loss of Trinity without flinching and immediately convert it into a colder victory by confirming the informant and naming the next target. The scene layer reads their coordination as the machine's totalizing surveillance turning outward — and their final image, the camera falling through the phone into a running 'search,' makes the collective itself the event's true endpoint, since the hunt no longer needs a body, only a name.

events.title: Neo is summoned and drawn toward the truth
events.summary: Alone in his apartment, Neo is contacted through his own machine by an unseen party that types messages on its own, answers a knock with the last line, and tells him to follow a white rabbit. When Choi and Dujour arrive for a disk deal, Neo spots a white rabbit pin on Dujour's jacket, and against his plan to work the next day he agrees to go out. At a crowded apartment gathering, Trinity approaches him by name, confirms she was on his computer, catalogs his private habits to prove she has been watching, warns him he is in danger and being watched, and reframes his sleepless searching as the hunt for an answer that is out there and will find him if he wants it, though it must be seen to be believed. She draws him in with a hypnotic, unhurried closeness over the deafening music, then melts back into the crowd, leaving him on his feet in the night, having named aloud the question What is the Matrix?.
events.action: The screens in Neo's apartment go blank and type messages on their own, answering a knock with the last line; Neo trades a disk to Choi for money, then follows Dujour out after recognizing the white rabbit pin; at the gathering, Trinity corners him against a wall and delivers a warning before disappearing into the crowd.

events.title: Neo's ordinary life reasserts itself
events.summary: The night's pull collapses into a mundane morning: an alarm clock drags Neo awake in his apartment, and he strains to read the clock-face, sees 9:15 A.M., and curses. The setting is then identified as the downtown office of Meta CorTechs, where Rhineheart lectures him about lateness and authority and delivers an either-or ultimatum about his job, to which Neo replies with flat, deferential compliance. The vast question Trinity raised is not answered or abandoned but crowded out by the immediate demand of the reprimand; he carries it still, pushed to the background by the mundane pressure of the workplace.

events.title: The Agents seize Neo at the office
events.summary: A routine package delivers a ringing phone and Morpheus's warning that forces are closing in, and the abstract threat becomes a real raid. Guided turn-by-turn by Morpheus's voice, Neo moves across the office floor — into an empty cubicle, down a row, into a first office on the left — and slips past the searching Agents to the base of the skyscraper, only to be driven to a window ledge he cannot bring himself to cross. When his nerve breaks and he climbs back inside, the way out is gone; a female employee points out his position, and the Agents take him, handcuffed and forced into a dark sedan.
events.action: The Agents seize Neo at the office and take him into custody, after his Morpheus-guided escape through the office floor ends in a failed crossing he cannot complete.

state_triples.reading: Neo acts throughout on a trust he cannot justify — he obeys a voice that has been hunting him through messages because the alternative, staying to learn what 'they' will do, is worse. His body follows each command even as his mind protests, and the whole sequence is a test of whether he can believe enough to be led. The ledge is where that faith breaks: he will risk the impossible only until the environment makes the danger feel real

state_triples.reading: Smith moves through the office as though the outcome is already decided — he enters Neo's cubicle himself rather than delegate, because he does not conceive of a way out of a sealed floor. That certainty is exactly what Neo exploits to get behind him, but it costs Smith nothing: his patience and his net are large enough that one evasion changes nothing. He is conducting, not chasing, and the capture at the end is the vindication of that composure rather than a relief.

Trinity's single curse is the measure of how much rests on Neo's escape — she is placed exactly where she can see it fail. Her dismay is not surprise at the raid but at its outcome: the man she has been steering toward the truth has been taken, and she can do nothing but witness it. The restraint of the reaction — one word, seen in a mirror

Her single gesture — turning and pointing out Neo's cubicle the instant the Agents arrive — is legible to everyone in the room but her own motive stays hidden, and that ambiguity is the whole point. She may be a knowing collaborator handing Neo over, or simply a startled coworker redirecting a frightening commotion toward its source; the scene refuses to decide, and so does Neo, who cannot tell whether he has been incidentally exposed or deliberately betrayed.

Morpheus guides with the calm of someone who has been waiting for this moment and means to use it — he tests Neo's readiness even in the middle of a raid, withholding explanation ('The answer is coming') and refusing to soothe beyond the facts. At the ledge he does not command; he lays out the two ways out and hands Neo the choice, then hangs up, because he believes fear, not incapacity

The phone is Neo's only tether to the one person trying to get him out, and its fall is the event's quiet turning point: from the moment it rings at his desk it is his lifeline, clutched through every command, and when the wind knocks it from his hand on the ledge he loses not just his balance but his guide. Its loss is what leaves him alone to decide — and alone to fail.

events.title: Neo is interrogated and implanted
events.summary: The Agents close in on Neo in the interrogation room. Smith lays out Neo's two lives and offers to wipe his record clean in exchange for Morpheus; Neo refuses with contempt, insults Smith, and demands his phone call. Smith drops the negotiation, asking what good a phone call is if Neo cannot speak, and Neo's mouth seals shut and melds smooth. The other Agents pin him down, and Smith animates a fiber-optic wire tap into an insect-fluke-worm creature that burrows into Neo's exposed navel.

events.title: Neo is reclaimed and taken to Morpheus
events.summary: A ringing phone wakes Neo — mouthless, shirt torn open, an implanted creature burrowing inside him — and a voice names him 'the One' and demands a single 'Yes.' He walks to the Adams Street bridge in the pouring rain, where a car slides to a stop; inside, Switch holds him at gunpoint while Apoc drives and Trinity insists the restraint is 'for our protection. From you.' When Switch stops the car and lays down 'Our way or the highway,' Neo opens the door to bolt, but Trinity reframes his flight as a road he has already been down and where it ends, and he closes the door and stays. The car then rushes off through the dark, wet streets, Neo half-dressed and rain-soaked, handed over to a war he has just consented to enter.

events.title: The Bug Removed
events.summary: In the moving car, Trinity seals an extractor over Neo's navel and, when suction alone fails to dislodge the tracker, she drives an electric charge through him to force it out; the fluke-like bug rockets through the coils into the glass cage, then reverts to a common wire tap when she tips it out onto the pavement behind the car, which carries on through the rain before halting in the alley behind Hotel Lafayette.
events.action: Trinity seals the extractor over Neo's navel and increases the suction; when that fails to catch the tracker, she fires an electric charge into him that drives the bug out through the coils into the transparent enclosure at the tubing's far end. She lifts the cage and tips the bug out the window onto the pavement, where it reverts to a common wire tap. The car drives on through the rain and pulls into the alley behind Hotel Lafayette.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: In the moving car, Trinity seals an extractor over Neo's navel and, when the gentler suction fails to catch the tracker before it burrows deeper, she electrocutes him to force it out; the fluke-like bug rockets into the glass cage and she dumps it into the night, where it reverts to a common wire tap as the car vanishes and later halts in the alley behind Hotel Lafayette.
prose_before_reconcile.action: Trinity seals the extractor over Neo's navel and turns up the suction while Switch feeds it power from the cigarette lighter; when the ultrasound shows the tracker slipping away, she overrides Switch's warning, fires a charge into Neo, and drives the bug out through the coils into the glass cage, then rolls down the window and drops it out. The car carries on through the rain and pulls into the deserted alley behind Hotel Lafayette.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The moment Trinity stops trying to coax the tracker out and electrocutes Neo to force it free — the point where saving him means hurting him.

events.title: The Red Pill
events.summary: Trinity brings Neo to room 1313 and warns him to be honest with the one who knows everything, then hands him off. Inside, Morpheus reframes Neo's lifelong, nameless dread as a real enslaving system and offers him a choice between forgetting and knowing; Neo swallows the red pill. The crew wires the trace program to him, and as they race to lock his location, the cracked oval dressing mirror liquefies and crawls into his body until he goes into cardiac arrest, at which moment Apoc secures the target and Morpheus calls for the signal that drags Neo out of the Matrix.
events.action: Trinity delivers Neo to room 1313 and tells him to be honest because 'He understands far beyond what you could ever conceive.,' then hands him to Morpheus. Morpheus recasts Neo's nameless anxiety as a real system of control and offers him the blue pill or the red pill; Neo chooses the red pill. Morpheus leads him into the equipment room, where the crew fixes the white electrode disks to him and hardwires the trace program; as Apoc hunts his signal, the cracked oval dressing mirror melts into a liquid gel that crawls over Neo and triggers fibrillation and arrest; Apoc locks the target just in time for Morpheus to call for the signal, and Neo is swallowed by darkness.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Trinity delivers Neo to room 1313 and warns him to be honest with the one who knows everything. Inside, Morpheus turns Neo's lifelong unease into a named enemy, then offers him a choice between forgetting and knowing; Neo swallows the red pill. The crew hardwires the trace program, and as they race to lock his location, the mirror liquefies and crawls into Neo's body until he goes into cardiac arrest, at which moment Apoc secures the target and Morpheus orders the signal that drags Neo into the
prose_before_reconcile.action: Trinity brings Neo to room 1313 and instructs him to be honest because 'He possesses knowledge beyond your comprehension.,' then hands him off. Morpheus reframes Neo's nameless dread as a real enslaving system and offers him the blue pill or the red pill; Neo chooses the red pill. Morpheus leads him into the equipment room where the crew wires him up, and as Apoc hunts his signal, the mirror melts into Neo and triggers fibrillation and arrest; Apoc locks the target just in time for Morpheus to call for the signal, and Neo is swallowed by darkness.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The choice of the red pill — the moment Neo swallows it rather than the blue one — which converts a reversible seduction into an irreversible extraction and makes the catastrophe of unplugging earned rather than inflicted.

events.title: Born Into the Real World
events.summary: In cardiac arrest, Neo ruptures the magenta amnion and stands bald and naked in the oval capsule of clear alloy, mirror gel crawling over his face. A machine severs the coaxial cable at the base of his skull and the clear plastic needle and cerebrum-chip, then vacuums him through the black hole into the waste line, where he slides through the sewer main and nearly drowns before a metallic cable snatches him up into a flying machine. Lowered onto the hovercraft floor half-conscious, he is helped up to face Morpheus, who names him Neo and welcomes him to the real world, and then he passes out.
events.action: The pod's amnion ruptures and Neo emerges bald and naked; the machine disconnects his coaxial cable and needle-chip, the vacuum pulls him through the waste line and sewer main, and the flying machine delivers him to the hovercraft, where Morpheus names him and the real world before he collapses.

events.title: Waking and Rebuilding
events.summary: Neo is recovered aboard the Nebuchadnezzar and brought back to consciousness, where Morpheus—certain they have found the one—has his body rebuilt and then begins dismantling his assumptions about himself and his era, leading him out to witness the reality rather than describe it.

Neo's arc here is the conversion of a body being done to into a mind trying to understand what is being done. Each answer Morpheus gives steadies him for a moment and then opens a deeper vertigo — needles become atrophied muscle, sore eyes become never-used eyes, and 1997 becomes a lost two centuries — until the only thing left is to follow the man who refuses to explain and instead promises to show.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Neo is pulled from the sewer and comes back to consciousness aboard the Nebuchadnezzar, where Morpheus, certain they have found the one they sought, has his body rebuilt and then begins to strip away his assumptions about himself and his time, leading him out to see the reality rather than describe it.
prose_before_reconcile.action: Neo wakes on the hovercraft floor, is moved to an operating table where Dozer and Morpheus rebuild his atrophied muscles, then wakes alone in a recovery room before Morpheus retrieves him and leads him up toward the main deck.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: Morpheus's decision to show the reality rather than explain it — the pivot from soothing a frightened new mind to demanding that Neo witness a truth too total to be described.

events.title: The Desert of the Real
events.summary: Morpheus leads Neo up a ladder to the main deck of the Nebuchadnezzar, then jacks him into the Construct and walks him through the truth of the Matrix: the world he knew is only a simulation, the sky was scorched, and humans are farmed for power. Neo resists every step, recoiling from the crew's touch as he comes to see them as agents of an unbearable violation, and when his mind cannot hold the truth his body speaks it — he thrashes against the restraints, tears free of the chair, screams at Trinity, Dozer, and Cypher to get away, then vomits and blacks out on the deck while the crew holds and tends him.
events.action: Morpheus initiates Neo into direct experience of the Matrix and narrates its history and horror while Neo's mind rebels and his body finally gives out.

state_triples.reading: Morpheus treats revelation as a discipline: he withholds nothing and comforts nothing, letting the images do the damage while his voice stays level. His faith in Neo outruns the evidence — he is wagering that this mind can survive what he is about to show it, and the wager nearly costs Neo his composure entirely.

Neo wants a definition he can stand on, and Morpheus gives him instead a vertigo: every category he reaches for is widened until there is nothing solid left. His refusal — 'It's not possible' — is the last defense of a world that no longer exists, and when his mind cannot hold the truth, his body speaks it for him

prose_before_reconcile.summary: On the main deck, Morpheus jacks Neo into the Construct and, over the next stretch of the ship's time, walks him through the truth of the Matrix — first reframing reality itself, then showing the scorched world, the fetus fields, and the power plant, before defining the whole system as control and reducing humanity to a coppertop battery. Neo resists every step, and when he demands to be let out, his body rejects the revelation on re-entry: the crew frees the cable, he collapses, and blacks out.

events.title: The Prophecy and the First of the Crew
events.summary: Recovered but spent, Neo lies awake in his dark room and accepts there is no going back; Morpheus enters, reframes the rescue as destiny by recounting the myth of the One and the Oracle's prophecy, then declares 'the search is over' before committing to guide him into training. Darkness gives way to flickering fluorescent light sticks in the hovercraft. Tank then enters as Neo's operator, shakes his hand, and — when Neo registers the missing jacks — explains that he and Dozer were born free in Zion, the last human city.
events.action: The event moves Neo from a physically spent survivor into an outwardly compliant recruit being oriented: Morpheus converts the trauma of the rescue into a prophesied purpose, and Tank supplies the first warm, human face of the world Neo has entered. The pivot belongs to Morpheus, whose declaration of belief repositions Neo from victim to instrument and sets the crew's mission in motion.

state_triples.reading: Neo is not yet a believer; he is a man testing the walls of a trap who has stopped screaming and started listening. His 'I can't go back, can I?' is asked from resignation, and his near-silence through the prophecy — no argument, only 'For what?' — reads as bracing rather than acceptance. With Tank he performs the ordinary ritual of the handshake and lets himself be led, extrapolating safety from warmth, but the missing jacks violate the only model of 'human' he has

events.title: The Sparring Program
events.summary: Tank skips the prescribed basics and loads combat programs straight into Neo, who absorbs kung fu and jujitsu in hours and comes out of the download convinced he now knows how to fight. Morpheus arrives, refuses to celebrate the claim, and submits it to a physical test in the dojo. Across a series of spars, Neo's furious, technique-driven assault is blocked and dismantled every time, until Morpheus beats him to the floor and insists that speed and even the air are not real forces — that this world answers to the mind, not the muscles. Neo's breakthrough comes not through understanding but through rage: he stops trying to perform technique and simply lands one clean blow on Morpheus, knocking his glasses off. Morpheus does not retaliate; he stops the spar and reframes himself as only a guide who can show the door, then orders Tank to load the jump program. The crew — Mouse, Tank and the rest — watch from the main deck as a spectacle, reading the fight's physiological signatures and confirming from the outside that what Neo is doing should not be possible.

events.title: The Jump
events.summary: Morpheus moves the session to a rooftop jump program to prove that the mind, not physics, governs the Construct, and crosses the gap himself to set the example. Neo runs and falls badly short, the yielding ground catching him, and on the main deck the crew watches the attempt split between doubters and believers while Trinity's quiet hope breaks her reserve and then she leaves before the aftermath. Tank seizes the disk and eases the plug from Neo, who is returned to his body injured, groaning, cradling his ribs and spitting blood into his hand. Morpheus guides Neo to name his own disbelief as the cause, then delivers the lethal corollary.
events.action: Morpheus converts a physical failure into doctrine: the mind makes the Matrix real and death there kills the body, and Neo is repositioned from a fighter who landed a blow into a trainee who has failed his first jump and just learned that failure there can kill him.

events.title: After Hours
events.summary: Trinity comes out of Neo's room having just been alone with the unconscious Neo in a way she can't own, and runs straight into Cypher watching her; she deflects his needling about her feelings without denying anything and leaves on her own terms, while Cypher—dressing up resentment over the dinner as a joke—fails to rattle her and reaches for the Oracle as a way to force Morpheus's faith into something verifiable, the first step away from loyalty.
events.action: Trinity steps out of Neo's room into the hall, meets Cypher's watch, and turns his suspicion back on him rather than putting anything personal on the record, then walks away and leaves the exchange on her own terms. Over the still, unconscious Neo, Cypher jabs that she never brought him dinner and presses that there is something about Neo; when she deflects instead of denying, he floats routing Neo through the Oracle so Morpheus's certainty can be tested—using the dinner as proof of a favoritism he resents and performing indifference so the probe doesn't look like what it is.

state_triples.reading: She has just been alone with Neo in a moment she would never let anyone witness, and the caretaking errand has tipped into something she can't quite own. Caught by Cypher a heartbeat later, her silence is less composure than the scramble to get that exposure off her face before she speaks; she deflects rather than denies because a flat denial would name what she is hiding. Her faith in Neo is the thing she has staked herself on

events.title: The Agent training program
events.summary: On a crowded downtown street that turns out to be a training program, Morpheus moves effortlessly through the jostling crowd while Neo is bumped and shouldered off the path, and reframes the ordinary people around them as the enemy. He stops the simulation around a gun-levelled Agent, leaving everything else frozen, and uses it to teach that Agents are sentient programs who can move into anyone still hardwired to the system. He tells Neo that every human who has fought one has died, but that Neo can surpass any Agent because their strength and speed are bound by rules while his are not.
events.action: Morpheus walks untroubled through the crowded downtown street as Neo is constantly bumped and shouldered, then freezes the program around a gun-levelled Agent and delivers the doctrine on what Agents are and the lethal stakes of fighting them, reframing Neo's weakness as a rule-bound limit he can overcome.

state_triples.reading: Neo is trying to rebuild his picture of reality faster than his fear will let him: every answer Morpheus gives ('This isn't the Matrix?', 'What are they?', 'Someone?') is a mind catching up, and the reflexive joke about dodging bullets is a reach back toward skepticism because believing the truth is more frightening than doubting it. He trusts Morpheus on awe and authority rather than understanding, and his sense of himself as an ordinary man lags badly behind what he is being told he is — the gap that Morpheus is betting he can close.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: On a crowded downtown street that turns out to be a training program, Morpheus reclassifies the Matrix's ordinary people as part of the enemy system, then uses Neo's distraction by a woman in a red dress to reveal that the crowd can become Agents — freezing the program as Agent Smith levels a gun at Neo's face. He explains that Agents are sentient programs who can inhabit anyone still plugged in, that every human who has fought one has died, and that Neo will succeed because their power is bound
prose_before_reconcile.action: Morpheus moves effortlessly through the crowd while Neo is constantly shoved aside and jostled from the way; Morpheus frames the businessmen, lawyers, teachers and carpenters as enemies, catches Neo staring at the woman in the red dress and turns it into a demonstration by freezing the program after Agent Smith appears, then delivers the doctrine on Agents and Neo's destined edge before his cell phone rings with trouble from Tank.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The program freezing on Morpheus's command — the moment the 'real' street reveals itself as a construct and Agent Smith's gun becomes a lesson rather than a death.

events.title: The Sentinel hunt and the ship's hiding
events.summary: A Sentinel sweeping the sewer main forces the Nebuchadnezzar into a tiny supply line too small for it, where Tank kills power and arms the E.M.P. as the ship's only weapon. The crew goes cold and silent, frozen in the darkened cockpit while the machine glides directly over them, then breathes again once it passes and disappears.

events.title: Cypher's disillusionment and his deal
events.summary: On the Nebuchadnezzar's main deck, Cypher pours Dozer's liquor for Neo and recasts Morpheus's prophecy as a body count, telling him five before him took on an Agent and died because Morpheus got them believing. Neo takes it as caution and retreats toward the ladder, shaken rather than converted. Cypher then crosses into the Matrix to a restaurant, where he savors an impossible steak and strikes a bargain with Agent Smith: his body returned to a power plant and reinserted as someone rich, important, and forgetful, in exchange for delivering the man who holds Zion's mainframe access codes. Smith names that man as Morpheus, and Cypher's private regret settles into reconciled treason.
events.action: Cypher pours two shots of Dozer's liquor for Neo on the main deck and reframes 'save the world' as a mindjob, revealing that five candidates before Neo confronted an Agent and died because Morpheus got them believing in bullshit. Neo drinks, reddens, and takes the warning to heart as caution, then turns for the ladder, leaving Cypher at the screens. Cypher meets Agent Smith in an upscale restaurant inside the Matrix, eats a steak he knows is not real, and lays out his terms: his body carried back to a power plant and reinserted into the Matrix as someone rich and important who remembers nothing. Smith presses only for commitment, then names the deliverable man as Morpheus, the one who carries the Zion mainframe access codes.

By the restaurant he has dropped the pretense of camaraderie and reduced himself to appetite, choosing the juicy lie over the grey real because being 'no one' in a cold ship has become unbearable. prose_before_reconcile.summary: Under cover of an initiation drink on the main deck, Cypher turns Neo's awe into seeded doubt, recasting Morpheus's prophecy as a body count of five dead candidates he watched die. He then meets Agent Smith in a restaurant and, over a steak he knows is not real, trades Morpheus for a rich, forgetful life back inside the Matrix, handing over the man who holds Zion's access codes. Regret hardens into open treason.
prose_before_reconcile.action: Cypher pours Dozer's liquor for Neo and reframes 'save the world' as a mindjob, revealing that five before him took on an Agent and died because Morpheus got them believing in bullshit. He then sits across from Agent Smith, savors an impossible steak, and lays out terms: his body returned to a power plant, reinserted into the Matrix as someone rich and important who remembers nothing. In exchange he delivers the man with the Zion mainframe access codes, and Smith names that man as Morpheus.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The pivot is Cypher choosing the comfortable lie over the unbearable real — his decision, voiced over the impossible steak, to trade Morpheus for oblivion, which converts his private disillusionment into an irreversible act of treason.

events.title: The crew goes in to reach the Oracle
events.summary: After the crew's gray breakfast, Morpheus singles Neo out to be taken to the Oracle. Tank launches the jump, and the crew materializes in the Hotel Lafayette before stepping back into the Matrix. As the others move toward the car, Cypher covertly connects a phone and drops it in a garbage can in the alley. During the drive, Neo grapples with the falseness of his memories and presses Trinity about what the Oracle told her, but she is struck physically mute at the moment of disclosure.

events.title: Entering the building and meeting the Oracle
events.summary: The party arrives at a vast tenement-like building understood as a place where people can disappear. Morpheus leads Neo up through it, into the elevator, down the hall, and to the Oracle's apartment door, while Neo follows and, at the threshold, backs away before committing. During the ascent, Neo presses Morpheus over the five failed candidates, and Morpheus confesses that he misunderstood the Oracle — that he had believed the prophecy was all about him and that he could anoint whoever he chose — admitting he was terribly wrong. He shifts from describing the Oracle in the abstract to disclosing that she personally told him he would find the One, and asks Neo to lean on residual respect and trust him until Neo can feel what he feels. Neo learns the Oracle is a fallible-sounding guide who knows enough rather than everything, and, among the Potentials, accepts the Spoon Boy's lesson that bending the spoon is impossible because there is no spoon — only oneself bends, the truth that reality here is a projection of the self, confirmed as he stares into the spoon and the reflected room slowly begins to bend. The Priestess opens the door before Neo touches it, greets him by name, and shepherds him through the household to the Oracle. Neo steps through the door into the Oracle's apartment, called forward to meet her while Morpheus is left behind, suspended between the terror of being the One and the safety of being a nobody.

events.title: The Trap Springs
events.summary: Neo leaves the Oracle carrying a private verdict and a death-prophecy he is ordered to keep. The crew regroups and moves toward extraction, but a repeated cat exposes that the Matrix is being rewritten around them, and the trap closes: Mouse is cornered and killed in Room 1313 while the rest of the group is sealed inside the Hotel Lafayette, forcing Morpheus to seize Trinity's traceable phone as their only play and to order Tank to find a structural drawing of the building.
events.action: The Oracle's verdict and warning are sealed into silence; the crew reassembles and heads for the exit; and the Matrix is rewritten around them so the extraction becomes an ambush. Mouse is killed and the survivors are trapped, which converts Morpheus from guide into a commander gambling with a traceable phone and directing Tank toward a structural way out.

state_triples.reading: She has arranged the whole encounter as a set of loaded choices rather than a fortune: she engineers the vase, softens 'not the One' with a cookie, and only then hands Neo the Morpheus prophecy after checking he truly wants it. So her grandmotherly performance is the instrument of a guide who is manufacturing a decision, not reporting a fate.

events.boundary_reason: This run is one continuous action — the crew's extraction interrupted by a Matrix-altered ambush — cutting between the hotel and the main deck as a single unit. It begins at sc-088, where the operators learn the crew is on their way, and the question becomes whether the crew escapes the trap. It runs through the deja vu glitch, the severed hardline, Mouse's death, and Morpheus taking command to find a way out. The final beat, Morpheus ordering Tank to find a structural drawing, closes the immediate reaction to being trapped and opens the escape plan; the next scene would answer a different question (how they get out), so the event ends here.

events.title: The escape into the plumbing wall
events.summary: As the police sweep the Hotel Lafayette floor by floor, Tank guides Morpheus by voice from the ship through the eighth-floor hall into Room 808, where the crew has smashed a man-sized hole into the main wet-wall; as Agent Smith relays the targets' location and the cops close in, the crew hides inside the wall and worms down the stack pipes to escape.
events.action: The police begin probing the rotting darkness of the Hotel Lafayette with flashlights and sweep the building floor by floor, flooding the eighth floor and rushing everywhere. On the ship, Tank, pulled back from helplessness by Morpheus's order, locates the structural drawing and feeds Morpheus the building's structure step by step, directing him left through the hall and into Room 808 to a spot confirmed directly in front of him. Meanwhile, Agent Smith stands over Mouse's body in Room 1313, raises his hand to his earpiece, and when the line clicks dead relays that the targets are on the eighth floor; Agent Brown begins receiving that relay as boots clatter up the marble staircase behind the police. The cops flood the eighth floor, sweep Room 808, and find it empty except for a person-width breach ripped through the wall covering and lath of the bathroom wall, while inside that wall the crew has concealed itself and is worming down the grease-black stack pipes.

prose_before_reconcile.action: The police begin searching the dark, decaying interior of the Hotel Lafayette floor by floor. On the ship, Tank pulls up the building's structural diagram and feeds Morpheus the schematics he demands, guiding him by voice through the eighth floor to a spot directly in front of him in Room 808. Meanwhile, Agent Smith stands over Mouse's body and relays to his fellow Agents that the targets are on the eighth floor; Agent Brown listens in the stairwell as boots clatter up behind the police, who flood the eighth floor and sweep Room 808, finding it empty except for a man-sized hole smashed through the bathroom wall. Inside that wall, the crew conceals themselves and descends the grease-black stack pipes.

events.title: The Agents close in; Morpheus sacrifices himself for Neo
events.summary: The Agents and cops converge on the crew's hiding place, and a firefight erupts inside the wall. When an Agent ambushes Neo in the crawlspace, Morpheus bursts through, pins the Agent down, and orders Trinity to get Neo out—choosing to give his own life so the others can escape.
events.action: Agent Brown, listening at his earpiece, stops concealing his purpose and openly demands to know where the people he is hunting are. Agent Smith, having relayed the targets' location from Room 1313 over Mouse's body, smashes through the plaster from the HALL into the WALL to ambush Neo, then is driven to the wet terrazzo floor and pinned in Morpheus's iron grip, unable to reach his weapon. Meanwhile the cops close in: one cop, searching and finding nothing, singles out a strange sound near the bathroom ahead of the others, and a Cop in ROOM 608, who had been pressing his ear to the plaster straining to make out whispers, hisses and a grunt, recoils as the wall bulges and shatter-cracks, now certain the fugitives are hidden inside it. He opens fire; inside the wall, Cypher loses his footing and is jammed between the wall and a cluster of heavy supply pipes in the line of fire, and Trinity pulls him free. Neo fires back through the plaster until the Cop, spinning for cover, freezes as something seizes him—his body spasming, his M-16 dropping. Then two arms smash through the wall and the Agent hurls Neo against the iron stack pipe, fingers at his throat. Morpheus, guided by Tank to Room 808, bursts through the plaster and lath into the WALL crawlspace, dives on top of the Agent, crashes with him to the wet terrazzo floor, and pins him choking, unable to reach his weapon. Morpheus shifts from request to command, ordering Trinity to get Neo out because Neo is all that matters. Trinity, torn and furious, accepts the order, drags the resisting Neo down and out, and the crew slides down the inside of the wall, fleeing and leaving Morpheus behind with the Agent.

events.boundary_reason: This run is the confrontation the previous flight was fleeing: the Agents take command of the hunt (sc-115), the cops track the fugitives into the walls (sc-116/sc-118), a firefight breaks out inside the wall (sc-119–sc-120), and it resolves with Morpheus pinning Smith and ordering Neo out — 'He is all that matters' — while the others flee (sc-121). sc-122 opens a new situation (the group crashing into the basement boiler room under grenade fire), so the boundary sits there.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: The Agents locate the crew's hiding place and a firefight erupts inside the wall; when an Agent ambushes Neo in the crawlspace, Morpheus pins him down and orders Trinity to get Neo out, trading his own life so the others can escape.
prose_before_reconcile.action: The Agents stand over Morpheus's abandoned jacket and demand the fugitives' whereabouts, then the cops close in on the wall—first one hears something near the bathroom, then a Cop presses his ear to the plaster, hears movement, and realizes the fugitives are hidden inside the structure itself just as it bulges and cracks. The Cop opens fire into the wall; inside, Trinity yanks Cypher free and Neo grabs his gun and blasts back through the plaster. The Cop spins for cover, then freezes as something seizes him, his weapon dropping while shadows rise from his flashlight. When gunfire fades, two arms smash through the wall and an Agent hurls Neo against the iron stack pipe, fingers gouging his throat. Morpheus bursts through and dives on the Agent, pinning him before he can reach his weapon, and commands Trinity to get Neo out because 'he is all that matters.' Trinity protests, drags the resisting Neo away, and the crew slides down the wall, leaving Morpheus behind with the Agent.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: Morpheus's decision to pin the Agent and order Trinity to get Neo out—trading his own life because 'he is all that matters.'

events.title: The group flees through the basement; Morpheus is captured
events.summary: In the basement's mechanical room, under grenade fire, Trinity stops searching the floor, finds the catch-basin cover, and pries the grate open so the survivors can descend; she reads Cypher's fall as an accident, but as a gas cloud envelops him he seems to trip and is lost, hidden by the gas smoke. Upstairs in Room 808, Morpheus starts dominant strangling Agent Smith, then loses ground — head-butting Smith but taking three head-butts back, a kick driving him into the wall, and a rush of cops burying him. Smith frees his throat, takes the blows unfazed with his nose and glasses shattered, and rises to order a wall of cops to seize Morpheus. On the ship, Tank reaches toward the screen and cries out in distress as Morpheus is taken.
events.action: The escape reaches its exit and the crew fragments: Trinity opens the way through the catch basin and the group descends, while Cypher is lost to the gas smoke. Simultaneously, Morpheus's one-on-one fight with Agent Smith reverses — he goes from strangling Smith to being driven into the wall and buried under cops, and Smith turns the brawl into a police action, ordering Morpheus captured alive. The flight ends and Morpheus is taken, shifting the situation from escape to capture.

events.summary: The crew re-establishes contact across two locations. Trinity climbs out of the WALL onto a back street with Neo. On the ship, Tank takes two calls—first Cypher, who demands an exit and is routed to a TV repair shop at Franklin and Erie, then Trinity, who identifies herself. Linking with Tank by radio, the street group learns Morpheus is alive but being moved to an unknown location, and that Cypher is already at the Franklin and Erie exit.
events.action: Trinity pulls Cypher free under fire, then climbs out onto the street and moves fast down a back street, leading Neo. On the ship, Tank answers a panicked call from Cypher, who needs an exit; a car crash has cleared his path, and Tank positions him at a TV repair shop at Franklin and Erie. Moments later Trinity calls and identifies herself. Out on the back street, Neo asks whether Morpheus survived; Tank, relayed through Trinity, confirms Morpheus is alive but being moved to an unknown location, then reveals Cypher is already at the Franklin and Erie exit.

events.title: Cypher's Betrayal
events.summary: Cypher turns quiet treachery into open murder aboard the ship: having shot Tank and left him for dead, he answers Trinity's call with a false story of an 'accident,' then, once the survivors are jacked back in, murders Apoc and Switch, delivers Morpheus to the Agents, and stands over the comatose Neo to force Trinity's answer—only to be struck down by Tank, who survived and returns armed.
events.action: sc-137 through sc-141. On the main deck, Cypher's first shot misses and he curses, then fires again, blasting Tank out of his chair and shooting him in the chest while Dozer cries out in horror from wherever he is watching. On the street, Trinity sends Neo to answer a ringing phone; he answers on a click and finds only dead silence, and Trinity moves to the cellular. Back on the deck the operator phone rings, and Cypher steps over Dozer's sizzling body to the monitor. Trinity reaches the line and Cypher answers by name, telling her Tank 'had an accident,' which shocks her. The crew returns to the ship, where Cypher, wearing Tank's operator headgear, stands over their jacked-in bodies, confesses he is tired of the war, and chooses the Matrix. He murders Apoc by yanking his plug, then Switch despite Trinity's pleas, explaining the Agents promised to reinsert him so he can wake up 'fat and rich.' He stands over Neo and demands Trinity say whether she believed Morpheus; she whispers 'yes,' and at that moment Tank—charred and bloody—levels the lightning gun and fires a bolt that knocks Cypher flying.

state_triples.reading: Tank's arc is one of stubborn survival: blasted and shot, he refuses to stay down, and his return is timed to the exact instant Cypher is about to kill Neo, answering the 'miracle' Cypher mocked. His silence until the last moment—announcing himself only with action and a curse—frames him as pure protective will, fighting for the ship and avenging his brother rather than reasoning with a traitor he has already judged.

Cypher moves from concealment to open declaration, and his cruelty is the pleasure of a man who resents the very freedom he is about to trade away. He packages murder as philosophy and grievance—'tired of this war'—and stages his betrayal as a vindication of being right about Morpheus. His fatal error is not moral but predictive: he taunts that a 'miracle' would have to stop him, and the miracle arrives in the form of the brother he thought he had already killed, so his certainty about Neo and Tank is what undoes him.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Cypher turns his quiet treachery into open murder aboard the Nebuchadnezzar, gunning down Tank and Dozer on the main deck while the crew tries to exit through a phone line he has severed. He then answers Trinity's call with a false story of an 'accident,' and, once the survivors are jacked back in, murders Apoc and Switch and delivers Morpheus to the Agents before being struck down by a surviving Tank.
prose_before_reconcile.action: sc-137 through sc-141. The event opens on the main deck as Cypher's first shot misses and he curses, then fires again, blasting Tank out of his chair and shooting him square in the chest while Dozer cries out in horror from wherever he is watching. On the street, Trinity sends Neo to answer the ringing phone; Neo answers on a click and finds only dead silence, and Trinity moves to the cellular. Back on the deck, the operator phone rings again and Cypher steps over Dozer's sizzling body to the monitor. Trinity reaches the line and Cypher answers by name, telling her Tank 'had an accident,' which shocks her. The crew returns to the ship, where Cypher, wearing Tank's operator headgear, stands over their jacked-in bodies and confesses he is tired of the war and chooses the Matrix. He murders Apoc by yanking his plug, then Switch despite Trinity's pleas, explaining the Agents promised to reinsert him so he can wake up 'fat and rich.' He stands over Neo, demanding Trinity say whether she believed Morpheus; she whispers 'yes,' and at that moment Tank—charred and bloody—levels the lightning gun and fires a bolt that knocks Cypher flying.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: Cypher's belief that Tank is dead and that no 'miracle' can stop him—so he takes his time over Neo to force Trinity's 'no'—is what gives the surviving Tank the instant he needs to return and fire.

events.title: The Survivors Escape and Wake
events.summary: Inside the TV repair shop, Neo rises to his feet, breaks free of Trinity's embrace, and sends her out first when the phone rings; then Trinity wakes aboard the ship on the Main Deck, is unplugged by Tank, and sits upright and aware. She names Dozer aloud and, reading the tightening of Tank's face, infers that he too is dead. Relief at waking safe gives way to grief as she takes Tank's wounds and loss into her arms, held under a low and controlled voice.
events.action: Neo revives and stands inside the construct, breaks Trinity's embrace, and directs her out first as the phone rings; Trinity then wakes on the Main Deck, is unplugged by Tank, sits upright, names Dozer, and reads Tank's silent reaction to understand that he is dead, before gathering him into her arms.

state_triples.reading: She wakes into relief and lets it be short, because the cost is already in front of her. She names only Dozer, but she reads Tank's face closely enough to take the whole loss in without making him speak it, and she answers with her arms rather than words — the same instinct that sent her to hold Neo moments before. She trusts silence, hers and his, to carry what saying aloud would make worse.

events.title: The Agents Take Morpheus Into Custody
events.summary: Agent Jones arrives on the government building's roof flanked by Marines and moves into the executive office, where Agent Smith is already holding Morpheus captive. Smith escalates the interrogation from cold philosophy to a doubled serum dosage that drives Morpheus's alpha pattern into an ordered wave — the sign he is about to break — while Morpheus spends his last agency fighting to keep his mind from cracking, believing he is alone. Aboard the Nebuchadnezzar's main deck, the crew confronts the choice of killing Morpheus to keep Zion's codes from the machines: Tank, charred and grieving Dozer, overrides Trinity's horror with the logic of necessity, and Neo, waking from the jack, refuses to accept that Morpheus has to die. The Agents then declare their man dead either way and convert the interrogation into a physical hunt by deploying the sentinels.

events.title: Neo Chooses to Rescue Morpheus
events.summary: The crew's wake is interrupted and reversed. Neo stops the plug from being pulled on Morpheus and commits to going back into the Matrix to bring him out alive. He denies being the One, so his mission becomes a wager on a man rather than a prophecy — something he cannot justify logically, only believe in. Trinity, gutted by both Morpheus's condition and Neo's self-denial, converts her grief into command and insists on joining as the ranking officer. Neo and Trinity arm themselves in the construct and jacking in, while Tank loads them into the Matrix. Across the two realities the interrogation sharpens: Smith, disgusted and coming unglued, isolates himself from Brown and Jones and threatens Morpheus with death for Zion's codes, while Tank settles beside Morpheus's failing body to urge him to hold on.
events.action: The decision becomes a plan. Neo demands guns; the construct arms him and Trinity; and Tank loads both of them into the Matrix. Meanwhile the interrogation sharpens across the two realities. Smith, disgusted and coming unglued, dismisses Brown and Jones and threatens Morpheus with death unless he yields Zion's codes. Tank, having been ordered to stand down from killing Morpheus, takes up his operator's station to load the rescue, then sits beside Morpheus's failing body, holding his hand and urging him to hold on.

state_triples.reading: Neo's turn is a surrender of the prophetic self in favour of a human one: he stops arguing to be the One and instead wagers his life on a belief he admits he cannot defend, and that wager — not destiny — is what frees him to act. Telling Trinity he is 'just another guy' is not despair but the ground he builds his courage on; he arms to the teeth precisely because he no longer expects to be protected. His terseness in the construct is the compression of a man who has stopped performing certainty for others and now simply moves.

Tank is the grieving son asked to do the unthinkable twice over — first to kill the father he mourns, then to enable a mission he believes is suicide — and his compliance is the measure of how completely Neo's faith has converted him. His 'besides a miracle' is not sarcasm but the honest register of a man who has surrendered logic to belief; sitting with Morpheus afterward, he has nothing left to argue and can only plead.

state_triples.reading: Smith's monologue about humanity as a disease is less an interrogation than a confession — he is describing the contamination he fears in himself. The anger that 'isn't supposed to happen to Agents' is the crack through which his private hatred of the Matrix pours out, and dismissing Brown and Jones is the moment he stops serving the collective and starts serving his own need to get out. His disgust at Morpheus's smell is displaced self-loathing; he needs the codes not for Zion but for an exit

Brown is the last voice of the collective's procedure, and his quiet reframe — 'perhaps we are asking the wrong questions' — is the only challenge Smith's failing method receives. He underestimates how far Smith has slipped, treating the anger as a manageable aberration, and the exchanged look with Jones is the unit's silent registration of a leader it no longer quite trusts. His dismissal marks the collective losing its hold on one of its own.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: The crew's wake is interrupted and reversed. Neo, seeing the plug about to be pulled on Morpheus, stops it and declares he is going back into the Matrix to bring Morpheus out alive. He confesses he is not the One, so his mission is a wager on a man rather than a prophecy, and he cannot justify it logically — he simply believes he can succeed. Trinity, gutted by both Morpheus's condition and Neo's shattering self-denial, converts her grief into command and insists on joining as the ranking offcer
prose_before_reconcile.action: The decision is turned into a plan: Neo demands guns, the construct arms them, and Tank loads Neo and Trinity into the Matrix. Meanwhile the interrogation across the two realities sharpens — Smith, disgusted and coming unglued, isolates himself from Brown and Jones and threatens Morpheus with death for Zion's codes, while Tank settles beside Morpheus's failing body to urge him to hold on.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: Neo's refusal to accept Morpheus's death — his insistence, against all logic and grief, that he can bring him back — which converts the crew's fatalism into a rescue and reverses the event's opening momentum.

events.title: The rescue of Morpheus and the escape from the building
events.summary: Trinity finishes loading the ability to fly a helicopter and the crew launches. Neo drops the helicopter onto the executive office and guns down Agents Jones, Brown and Smith, then finds Morpheus unresponsive and has to extract him by force. As Morpheus revives and bolts for the window, Smith shoots him in the leg mid-dive, but Neo leaps after him and catches his handcuffed wrist before he hits the ground. Trinity swings the machine toward the nearest roof; both men land, yet the slack rope drags Neo toward the edge until he levers onto the rain gutter and Trinity shoots the cord, freeing him as the helicopter smashes into a glass skyscraper and explodes, leaving Trinity swinging against a shatterproof window.
events.action: The rescue of Morpheus and the escape from the building. Trinity completes the helicopter download and the crew moves. Neo strafes the executive office from the hovering helicopter, destroying Agents Jones, Brown and Smith, then has to rouse and physically extract an unresponsive Morpheus. Morpheus revives and runs for the window; Smith, reconstituted, shoots him in the leg as he dives, but Neo hurls himself after him and seizes his handcuffed wrist before he falls to the ground. Trinity throws the dying, shot-up helicopter toward the nearest roof — both men drop and roll free — but the slack rope drags Neo toward the edge until he levers onto the rain gutter and Trinity shoots the cord, freeing him as the helicopter smashes into a glass skyscraper and explodes, leaving Trinity swinging against a shatterproof window.

state_triples.reading: Trinity enters this event as the one who has turned the crew's awe into a plan, and the download makes her the literal driver of the escape. Her arc is control tested and then stripped away: she flies with command until the machine dies under Smith's fire, and the involuntary 'Shit-shit-no!' is the only crack in a composure that otherwise never stops acting. That crack matters because it exposes how much she has at stake — she does not just fly them out, she lunges one-handed for the rope and shoots to free Neo

state_triples.reading: Jones is the embodiment of the Agents' certainty walking into a reality that has already overtaken it. He enters first and unhesitating, still carrying the predatory momentum of pinning Neo on the roof, and that same leading-charge aggression makes him the first to die — he is killed precisely because he treats the flooded office as just another hunting ground, not recognizing that Neo now holds a mounted gun from a helicopter. His death is the event's first proof that the Agents' invulnerability has ended.

Smith is the event's through-line of thwarted control. He begins as one of three Agents holding Morpheus in the executive office, comprehends the attack with a coldness that suggests mastery, and is gunned down last — knowledge granting him nothing. Reconstituted, he does not retreat into procedure but into fury: the 'Nooo!' is the crack of a being who has now twice lost the One's mentor, and his sweeping fire is area-denial desperation, not a clean kill-shot. By the escape he is reduced to mechanical persistence — he cannot stop the flight.

state_triples.reading: Neo's arc across this event is the film's faith-in-him thesis made physical. He begins as the man on the machine gun who cleared the rooftop, but inside the office he is helpless before the one thing firepower cannot fix — an unresponsive Morpheus — and has to shift from willing him to move to moving him himself. He judges 'He won't make it' and then overrides his own calculation by hurling his body into empty space, becoming the anchor. The crash then tests him again: he is dragged like a skipping stone and saves himself on the gutter

state_triples.reading: Morpheus moves from the ultimate passivity — a mind and body being dismantled — to a sudden, furious reclamation: the eyes 'dark and flashing with fire' signal will returning all at once, and he converts it straight into motion, snapping the cuffs and running without a word to anyone. His escape is real but immediately punished — Smith's bullet in the leg turns the dive into a fall — so that his survival is no longer his own doing but Neo's: the mentor who refused to break is now literally held by the student he doubted. He ends the event reduced to what

physical.entry: present but not described as affected
physical.exit: Blistering with snow-static in the hall outside the executive office.

state_triples.reading: The three Marines are a beat of pure texture rather than agency — they stand in the hall and blister with snow-static, a visual signal that the Matrix is destabilizing around the crew's incursion. They neither act nor react

The snow-static is the visible sign of the Matrix breaking down around the Marines as the crew's rescue tears through the simulation's stability — a textural marker of corruption rather than an agent of the plot.

The bolted bar is the anchor Neo clips the rope to before leaping — a fixed point that lets him bet his body on Morpheus. It holds through the collision and the snap, the one immovable thing in a scene of falling bodies.

The window is the breached boundary of the Agents' sanctuary — blown inward by Neo's gunfire to become the entry of the attack, then the exit of the escape as Morpheus dives through it and Smith fires back out through it. It is the threshold the rescue turns inside out.

The handcuffs are the physical token of Morpheus's captivity, and their journey traces the rescue: snapped free of the chair, they stay on his wrists as he falls, and it is precisely the still-cuffed wrist that Neo snatches out of the air. The restraint that marked him as a prisoner becomes the handle by which he is saved.

The helicopter is the crew's fragile conveyance — loaded with purpose in Trinity's hands, it carries the rescue aloft and then dies under Smith's fire, its failing engine and pouring oil forcing the crash-landing that nearly costs Neo. Its destruction is the event's final beat of mechanical jeopardy, the machine that saved them becoming the thing that almost kills one of them.

Smith's gun is the persistent mechanical menace of the escape — it wounds Morpheus in the leg mid-dive and then keeps firing through the rain until it kills the helicopter. It is the physical expression of Smith's refusal to let the quarry go, the threat that follows the crew out of the building and into the sky.

The climbing rope is the event's most versatile object — first the lifeline Neo clips to the bolted bar to catch Morpheus, then the umbilical that nearly drags Neo to his death when the helicopter falls, and finally the cord Trinity shoots to free him. It binds the rescue and the jeopardy together: the same line that saves Morpheus endangers Neo, and only Trinity's shot severs the knot.

The rain gutter is the small, fixed thing that saves Neo — the ledge his feet find as he is dragged toward the edge, letting him lever up just before Trinity cuts the cord. It is the narrow margin between being pulled over with the crashing helicopter and getting back on his feet.

Trinity's gun is the instrument of her last-second rescue — drawn one-handed while she grabs the rope with the other, she fires to sever the cord and free Neo from the crashing helicopter. It is the decisive action that closes the event's final jeopardy, the shot that turns a death into a survival.

The glass skyscraper is both the intended landing roof and the crash site — Trinity throws the dying helicopter toward the nearest building, and it smashes blades-first into this glass tower and explodes. It is the spectacular end of the escape vehicle, the structure that absorbs the machine's destruction while the crew survives on the adjacent roof.

prose_before_reconcile.action: The rescue of Morpheus and the escape from the building. Trinity completes the helicopter download and the crew moves. Neo strafes the executive office from the hovering helicopter, destroying Agents Jones, Brown and Smith, then has to rouse and physically extract an unresponsive Morpheus. Morpheus revives and runs for the window; Smith, reconstituted, shoots him in the leg as he dives, but Neo hurls himself after him and seizes his handcuffed wrist before he falls to the ground. Trinity throws the dying, shot-up helicopter toward the nearest roof — both men drop and roll free — but the slack rope snaps taut and drags Neo toward the edge until he levers onto the rain gutter and Trinity shoots the cord, freeing him as the helicopter smashes into a glass skyscraper and explodes, leaving Trinity swinging against a shatterproof window.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The pivot is Neo's leap after Morpheus — the instant he overrides his own judgment that 'He won't make it' and hurls his body into empty space to catch his mentor by the handcuffed wrist. Everything before it is about clearing the room; everything after is about whether that bet holds through the坠落.

events.title: Aftermath on the roof: belief confirmed and an exit arranged
events.summary: In the rescue's aftermath, Tank's watch resolves into certainty about the One; Neo tries to report what the Oracle told him, but Morpheus cuts him off and reinterprets both the prophecy and Trinity's silence as confirmation; then a call to the ship secures an exit, and Morpheus and Neo set out toward it.
events.action: Watching from the ship, Tank moves from uncertainty to certainty and exclaims that the man on screen is the One. On the rooftop, Morpheus asks Trinity whether she believes, and she answers only by looking at Neo rather than in words. Neo begins to report what the Oracle told him, but Morpheus cuts him off, insisting she said only what he needed to hear and that Neo will in time learn the gap between understanding a route and actually traversing it it. Morpheus then contacts Tank for an exit; Tank reports one already ready at the subway at State and Balbo, and Morpheus says they are on their way.

Every impossible outcome becomes proof, and his compression of feeling into purpose on the exit call is the same refusal to let anything destabilize the prophecy.

events.title: The Agents track the escapees; Smith senses something
events.summary: On the rooftop, Brown reports that the trace has fixed the crew's position and Jones orders a Sentinel strike against it; Smith withdraws from the unit in disgust, insisting the quarry is not gone. In a subway station below, Morpheus answers a ringing phone and exits through the line first, while Neo puts Morpheus through ahead of himself and an old drunk watches the vanishing with sudden, glowing-eyed recognition. Back on the roof, Smith starts to turn away, then is jolted back to attention by a sound, head whipping around to stare.
events.action: The rooftop pursuit closes the trap: Brown supplies the completed trace, Jones converts it into a strike order, and the Sentinels are loosed against the crew's known position. Smith, refusing a tidy procedural win, breaks from the unit at the building's edge and declares the targets still in play. The event then cuts to the escape: Neo, Trinity and Morpheus reach a subway station, Morpheus answers the ringing phone and disappears through the line first, and a shadowed old man reacts to the impossible sight with eyes that flare white. The thread returns to Smith, whose resignation is interrupted by a sound that snaps his attention back mid-turn.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: On the rooftop the three Agents confirm the trace has fixed the crew's position and Jones orders a Sentinel strike, but Smith breaks from the unit in disgust, insisting the quarry is not gone. Below, in a subway station, Morpheus answers a ringing phone and exits through the line while an old drunk watches his vanishing with sudden, glowing-eyed recognition. Back on the roof, Smith—convinced he will never be rid of the Matrix—starts to turn away, then is jolted back by something he hears, headsn
prose_before_reconcile.action: The rooftop pursuit closes the trap: Brown reports the completed trace, Jones converts it into a strike order, and the Sentinels are loosed on the crew's known position. Smith, unable to accept a tidy procedural win, withdraws to the building's edge and contradicts them, declaring the targets still in play. The event then shifts to the escape: Morpheus, Neo and Trinity reach a subway booth, Morpheus goes first and disappears through the phone, and a shadowed old man reacts to the impossible sight with eyes that flare white. The thread returns to Smith, whose hatred and resignation are interrupted by a sound that snaps his attention back, mid-turn.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The pivot is Smith's certainty that the quarry is not gone — a conviction the event vindicates when a sound arrests him mid-departure, confirming that his obsession, not the unit's procedural calm, tracks the truth.

events.title: The subway escape; Neo is trapped with Smith
events.summary: A train's roar and strobing light cover Agent Smith's reveal from the drunk in the corner and his shot at Trinity; she vanishes through the phone line a breath before the bullet lands, leaving only a shattered booth behind. Ripped back into the hovercraft, Trinity demands to be sent back to Neo, but Tank refuses—he cannot. Left alone in the subway station, Neo turns to face Smith, who has the gun trained on him and names him by his planted name.
events.action: The train's noise and strobing light mask the moment the old man in the corner becomes Agent Smith, who raises the black gun-metal and fires at Trinity as she lifts the receiver. She jacks out through the phone line just before the bullet passes through the booth, shattering the plastic window and the handset's ear-piece and leaving the booth empty and wrecked. Trinity jolts back into the hovercraft, alert and desperate to return to Neo, but Tank—blindsided by the broken feed and now knowing only that an Agent attacked Neo—refuses, because he cannot send her back. In the subway station, Neo is left cut off from her, turning to face Smith with the gun aimed at him.

events.title: The crew watches as Neo decides to stand and fight
events.summary: Aboard the ship's Main Deck, Morpheus, Trinity and Tank watch the scrolling code while Neo stands alone in the subway station before a dead escalator. Trinity, having been brought back aboard from the rooftop, urges Neo to run; Neo does not run. He turns back from the escalator to face the hunter and hardens into a fixed, gunfighter's calm. On the deck, Morpheus reads that stillness as the beginning of belief, while Trinity can only register it as something she cannot understand.
events.action: The event cuts between two places at once: the Main Deck, where Morpheus and Trinity stand behind Tank, bound to the cascading code., and the subway station, where Neo stands alone. Trinity, no longer on the rooftop but safe aboard the ship, breaks her silence to speak urgently into the connection, repeating her command for Neo to run, then falls back into a flat, puzzled question she cannot answer. Neo does not run; he looks up at the dead escalator, turns back, and his eyes settle into something fixed and hard — a gunfighter's calm with no past or future. On the deck, Trinity cannot map what she is seeing onto anything sensible, and Morpheus answers that Neo is beginning to believe.

events.title: Neo and Smith's subway battle; Neo seizes his power and runs
events.summary: After their gunfight ends in a mutual empty click, Neo and Agent Smith trade bare-handed blows until Smith chokes Neo near the electrified third-rail and uses the arriving train to frame his death as settled inevitability; at the edge of death Neo refuses the name and fate Smith pronounces, summons an impossible surge, hurls Smith into the tunnel ceiling, and breaks free as the train barrels over him—only for Smith to burst from the last car, glasses intact, and resume the chase as Neo runs, limping, for the escalator.
events.action: The gunfire ends in a mutual empty click, and Smith, enraged at being matched, switches to fists, cutting Neo's forearm and slamming him against a column before Neo lands a neck-snapping round-house that sends Smith's glasses flying. In the hovercraft, Trinity watches Neo's real body jerk and cough blood and realizes someone is killing him. Back in the station, Smith drives Neo toward the electrified third-rail, then uses the arriving train to stage the kill, choking him and forcing him to face the headlight he calls 'the sound of your death.' Unable to breathe and refusing to die, Neo names himself, then impossibly hurls Smith into the ceiling and backflips clear as the train explodes into the station. He runs for the escalator, but the train stops and Smith bursts from the last car in furious pursuit, his glasses intact.

state_triples.reading: Neo is fighting two battles at once: the physical one he is losing, and the internal one over whether he will accept the name and fate his enemy assigns. His two words, 'My name is Neo,' are not a plea but a refusal to be the killable 'Mr. Anderson' Smith pronounces him to be, and the impossible surge that follows is the first true eruption of the One—not a tactic but an identity breaking the rules he was born under. Yet he still believes escape ends the threat, which is why he runs toward the hallway where Smith will ambush him

state_triples.reading: Smith's rage is the tell: for the first time an 'inferior' human has matched him, and the insult to his supremacy wounds him more than any blow. He responds by reframing the fight as natural law—lecturing Neo about inevitability, forcing him to watch the headlight, pronouncing his death like a clerk closing a file—because he cannot tolerate parity. His certainty that Neo is a fixed, nameable quantity is precisely the arrogance the scene punctures, and his composed emergence with glasses intact signals he was never truly undone

events.title: The Crew Lose Neo and the Sentinels Arrive
events.summary: In the hovercraft, Tank loses Neo on the screen. A siren sounds; Morpheus, who had begun interpreting events for the crew, breaks off and bolts for the ladder into the cockpit. There he reads the sentinels on the radar, gives the crew five or six minutes, and orders Tank to charge the E.M.P. Tank, who had lost the feed, converts his alarm into pure compliance and charges the weapon. Trinity, having just watched Neo's body jerk and cough blood, moves into the cockpit behind Morpheus and objects that Neo must be out before the E.M.P. is used; Morpheus answers 'I know, Trinity' and reassures her that Neo will make it.
events.action: The crew's search for Neo inside the Matrix is overtaken by a real-world emergency: the siren drives Morpheus to the cockpit, where he reads the incoming sentinels on the radar and orders the E.M.P. charged, overriding Trinity's insistence that Neo be out first.

state_triples.reading: Tank is the operator who cannot afford to hesitate: the one word the siren wrings out of him is the only crack, and from then on he converts that jolt into pure compliance, because a fumbled charge kills everyone. He stays out of the moral collision between Morpheus and Trinity entirely, treating the order as procedure alone.

state_triples.reading: Morpheus moves with no wasted motion from interpretation to defense, and once he sees the sentinels his priorities reorder entirely to the ship's survival — yet when Trinity protests he answers 'I know, Trinity,' acknowledging her point rather than correcting it, because the believer who anointed Neo as the One cannot afford to act as though his loss is certain. His reassurance that Neo will make it is something more than optimism, grounded in the prophecy he has invested his life in, and it is precisely this that lets him steady the crew without fract.

affects_outside.enables: The E.M.P. charge puts the ship's only defense on a timer, so that when Neo is ambushed and shot moments later, the crew's ability to save him is now boxed in by a countdown that did not exist before this event.
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It forecloses any unhurried reckoning with what happened to Neo inside the Matrix; his fate is subordinated to the sentinels' approach, and Trinity's need for an answer about whether he is alive is left deliberately unanswered.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: Neo, still jacked in and fleeing toward an exit, is the unseen party the whole deadline is measured against — the order to charge the E.M.P. turns his flight into a race he does not know he is running.

events.turns_on: Whether the E.M.P. can be made ready without being fired on Neo before he is out — and whether Morpheus's faith that Neo will make it is right.

prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: Whether the E.M.P. can be made ready without being fired on Neo before he is out — and whether Morpheus's faith that Neo will make it is right.

events.title: Neo's Flight Through the City to the Fire Escape
events.summary: Neo snatches the BUSINESSMAN's cell phone mid-sprint and raises the crew, then runs a gauntlet that tightens at every block: his call becomes a demand for extraction, the demand becomes a running report as Smith closes to point-blank range, the open market fills with Agents at every turn, and a dead-end alley forces him to kick his way through an apartment building while Tank steers him by voice. He breaks a locked door, gets redirected twice, dives through a window as a knife pins the casing, drops down a fire escape, and lands broken and bleeding, still not out.
events.action: Neo snatches the BUSINESSMAN's cell phone and dials long distance while sprinting; on reaching the crew he demands extraction, then reports his pursuit to Tank. Smith gains on him, stops, and fires, shattering Neo's reflection in a truck mirror; Neo careens into a market ringed by Agents, dives into a dead-end alley and cries for help, then forces a locked door and lunges clear of gunfire. Steered by Tank's voice he kicks the wrong door, whirls to his other left through a bullet-riddled door, and leaps for the fire escape as a knife buries itself in the casing; he tumbles down the fire escape with Agent Brown a breath behind him, lands broken and bleeding, and charges for the end of the alley.

events.title: Recognition and the Sentinel Ambush
events.summary: Two recognitions land at once. Across from the Heart O' The City Hotel, Agent Smith is passing when the place suddenly registers with him and his focus locks onto its faded neon sign, fixing him at the point of identification without yet acting. Aboard the Nebuchadnezzar in the sewer main, Tank loads the exit and commits to making the call while Morpheus drives the escape — but the lights go red, the sentinels slam down onto the hull, and the ship passes in an instant from a refuge running an extraction to a vessel under direct physical assault, leaving Morpheus at the EMP detonator as the only move left.
events.action: Agent Smith halts outside the Heart O' The City Hotel, his attention fixing on the building's faded neon sign as something there registers with him, moving him from an unregistered pass to the point of recognition. Inside the Nebuchadnezzar, Tank loads the exit and declares he is going to make the call, fully committed to connecting the line. Morpheus is at comms ordering the escape through when the lights go red; he names the pursuers' arrival as the ship is struck, then moves to the EMP detonator and opens its lock. The sentinels slam down onto the hull, and by the impact the ship has become a breached vessel under direct assault, with the EMP unlocked and ready in Morpheus's hands as the only remaining counter.
