prose_before_reconcile.summary: Across the hotel, the sewer, and the ship, a single reversal lands: a hunter recognizes the place his quarry has chosen to hide, and at the same instant the hunters physically reach the ship. The crew's escape, already at its last second, is arrested by that arrival — the red lights, the impact on the hull, the EMP being readied as the only move left. What begins as a beat of recognition ends as an open fight for survival.
prose_before_reconcile.action: Agent Smith halts outside the Heart O' The City Hotel, his attention fixing on the building's faded neon sign as something there registers with him. Inside the Nebuchadnezzar, Tank loads the exit and declares he is going to make the call, and Morpheus orders him to do it — but the lights go red, Trinity says no, and Morpheus names the pursuers' arrival. The sentinels then slam down onto the ship in the sewer main. On the impact, Morpheus unlocks the EMP detonator., ready to deploy it, and says that Neo is going to make it while Trinity watches.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The escape is arrested by the arrival of the hunters — the forward momentum of getting Neo out is snapped into sudden jeopardy the instant the lights go red and the ship is struck, converting the whole situation from 'will they get him out' to 'they are here.'

events.title: Neo's Flight to the Phone
events.summary: Neo climbs a fire escape under fire in the alley while two Agents close the gap behind him; the chase cuts to a man breaking through a third-floor window into a hall, then to the hovercraft where Tank reports a hull breach and Trinity drives Neo to hurry, then back to the hall where Neo races toward door 303 and is stopped cold by Agent Smith's point-blank shot.
events.action: Neo scrambles up the fire escape as bullets spark and ricochet around him and the two Agents close the gap behind him. The chase shifts to the third floor, where a man kicks in a window and lands inside the hall as the door numbers count down. On the main deck, Tank reports that the attackers have burned through the outer hull and Trinity compresses the shrinking time into a single command to hurry. Back in the hall, Neo runs toward door 303, and just as he throws it open he finds Agent Smith waiting with a cocked .45; he freezes, unable to move or think, and the gun fires at point-blank range.

events.title: Death, the Kiss, and the Miracle
events.summary: In the Matrix, Agent Smith shoots Neo three times in the chest in the hall and Agent Brown confirms him gone; in the real world, the life monitors flatline and the crew gives him up even as sentinels breach the hull. Trinity refuses the ending: she takes hold of his body and kisses him, and the monitors jump back to life. Neo's eyes snap open, and Morpheus, who had reached for the EMP in weeping despair, is left with his faith overturned.
events.action: Agent Smith moves from outside the Heart O The City Hotel into the third-floor hall, stands over Neo's body at door 303, and shoots him three times in the chest; Neo drops to the blue shag carpeting and his body jerks as the life monitors flatline. Agent Brown checks the vital signs and reports the confirmed verdict, 'He's gone,' and Smith dismisses him with a smile and 'Good-bye, Mr. Anderson.' Aboard the hovercraft, sentinels sear through the main deck and slice open the hull while the crew grieves. Morpheus recoils in denial, then weeping takes hold of the EMP switch. Trinity moves from the comms to Neo's body, kisses him, and the monitors jump back to life; she screams for him to get up. Neo's eyes snap open and he returns to awareness in the chair on the main deck.

state_triples.reading: Neo is the pivot of the whole event and its only true mover: he dies as an ordinary man, shot in a hallway and confirmed gone, and comes back as something the crew can only call a miracle. The scenes give him no interior voice — he does not think or speak his way back; he is acted upon, loved back, and then simply opens his eyes. That silence is the point: his becoming is something that happens to him and around him, not something he chooses yet.

events.boundary_reason: These scenes form one unit — the crew's reaction to Neo's flatline, Trinity's declaration of love and kiss, and the monitors roaring back to life — all answering whether Neo is truly gone. prose_before_reconcile.summary: Two deaths are declared at once — in the Matrix, Smith shoots Neo three times and Brown confirms him gone; in the real world, the life monitors flatline and the crew gives him up as the hull is breached. Trinity refuses the ending: she takes his body, tells him the Oracle's words, and kisses him believing he will feel it. The monitors jump back to life, and she screams for him to get up.
prose_before_reconcile.action: Neo is shot three times in the chest in the hall and falls; his body jerks on the main deck as the life monitors flatline. Sentinels slice open the hull while the crew grieves. Brown checks the body's vital signs and reports "He's gone," and Smith bids "Good-bye, Mr. Anderson." Trinity takes hold of Neo's body, whispers the Oracle's prophecy and that she loves him, and kisses him. The monitors come back to life; Trinity screams for Neo to get up. An unnamed man in the hotel hall opens his eyes.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: Trinity's kiss — the moment she stops grieving and acts on the Oracle's words, refusing to let the flatline be final. It is the hinge between the two declared deaths and the miracle that undoes them.

events.title: The One Awakens
events.summary: Revived in the hotel hall, Neo halts the Agents' volley with a raised hand and begins reading the room as flowing code; aboard the Nebuchadnezzar the crew watches him blaze across the screens and Morpheus declares him the One, moments before an explosion rocks the ship; back in the hall Neo enters Agent Smith and bursts out of him, destroying the first Agent ever, so the surviving Agents feel fear for the first time and flee.
events.action: Neo rises in the hall and stops the three Agents' gunfire midair with a raised hand, studies a bullet's reflection, lets the rounds fall, and reads the room as a stream of code. Agent Smith, refusing to believe it, orders the others to fire, and their certainty cracks when the bullets do nothing. Aboard the Nebuchadnezzar, Tank, Morpheus, and Trinity watch the scrolling code resolve into live vividly colored shots of Neo standing in the hall; Tank can only stammer how, and Morpheus answers with exultant certainty that Neo is the One, before an explosion shakes the whole ship. In the hall, Smith screams and charges; Neo sinks into him and bursts out of his body, exploding him into light until only Neo remains. The remaining Agents exchange a single look and run.

state_triples.reading: Neo's return is not merely survival but a change in what he is: the fear that governed him is gone, and his lack of fear is the revelation. He does not fight the guns so much as refuse them, and the calm with which he studies his own reflection in a halted bullet is the first true act of the One. Yet his immunity reads as permanent only because he cannot yet see how the system will adapt beyond this hall.

His whole model of Neo, and of the world that made him its enforcer, is falsified in a single glance, and his rage is the last reflex of a certainty that has already lost.

state_triples.reading: For Morpheus the images are not a puzzle to solve but a prophecy confirmed, and his doubled 'He is the one' is a man steadying himself against the intensity of a faith made visible. His wonder is religious, not analytical; he hears his own certainty as the answer to Tank's 'How...?!' when it actually sidesteps the question. The event validates the belief he has held all along, at the very moment it seemed impossible.

Trinity's stake in the miracle is personal, not prophetic — where Morpheus sees the One, she sees the man she called back. Her silence here is not absence but absorbed feeling, the payoff of her desperation moments before, and it is legible only through what she did when the monitors first returned. What she cannot yet know is the nature of the change in him, that he now commands the Matrix in ways that will reshape what he is to all of them.

events.title: The Escape
events.summary: Sentinels overrun the ship's main deck, jolting Trinity from awe at Neo's return into a single, urgent summons to get up. In a hall, a man who has only been hearing a woman's voice reacts to a ringing phone and charges toward its source. Back on the deck, a sentinel descends on Morpheus at the EMP switch; on a screen Neo appears as a rushing stream of code diving for the phone, and at Trinity's 'Now!'—timed to that dive—Morpheus turns the key. A searing burst of brilliant white light engulfs the chamber. overflow pit, and the sentinels blink and fall dead, their cold metal carcasses filling it.
events.action: The event runs as one coordinated beat across three spaces. On the main deck the sentinels' destruction of the ship converts Trinity's awe into a single, desperate summons, lifting her from over Neo's body into the open, exposed deck. Simultaneously, in the hall, the man moves from only hearing the woman's voice to physically rushing toward the ringing phone. The two threads converge back on the deck: with a sentinel closing on Morpheus, Trinity's 'Now!' times his turn of the key to Neo's dive for the phone on the screen, and the resulting surge floods the overflow pit with white light and kills the sentinels.

state_triples.reading: Trinity is the event's conductor: her awe at Neo's return is cut short by the attack, and she converts panic into timing, holding the moment until Neo reaches the phone and only then releasing Morpheus. Her single 'Neo!' and her 'Now!' bracket the whole escape

events.boundary_reason: Trinity's call, Neo diving for the phone, Morpheus turning the key, and the EMP wiping out the sentinels are one continuous action — the crew's escape from the disabled ship. The boundary at sc-219 is the renewed sentinel assault that interrupts the awe of the previous event; the boundary at sc-223 is where the danger is over and the story settles into the quiet aftermath aboard the still hovercraft.

prose_before_reconcile.summary: Sentinels overrun the ship's main deck, and Trinity's single summons cuts across the destruction. In a hall, a man who has been hearing a woman's voice reacts to a ringing phone and rushes toward it. Back on the deck, a sentinel closes on Morpheus at the EMP switch; on a screen Neo dives for the phone, and at Trinity's 'Now!' Morpheus turns the key. A searing burst of white light engulfs the overflow pit and the sentinels fall dead, their carcasses filling it.
prose_before_reconcile.action: The event runs as one coordinated beat across three spaces. On the main deck the sentinels' assault forces Trinity from awe at Neo's awakening into a desperate summons. Simultaneously, in the hall, the man moves from only hearing the woman's voice to physically charging the ringing phone. The two threads converge back on the deck: with a sentinel descending on Morpheus, Trinity's 'Now!' times Morpheus's turn of the key to Neo's dive for the phone, and the resulting surge kills the sentinels in the overflow pit.
prose_before_reconcile.turns_on: The escape hinges on Trinity's 'Now!' — the instant she releases Morpheus's turn of the key in exact time with Neo's dive for the phone on the screen.

events.title: A New World
events.summary: In the darkened hovercraft, Trinity's vigil breaks: Neo wakes at her voice, reaches for her, and she weeps as she kisses him, releasing the grief she held while watching over his body. The scene then shifts to Neo standing alone in a hall, unharmed and transformed, before he moves into a phone booth on a city street and rises into open flight above the skyscrapers. Speaking from inside the Matrix, no longer running or hiding, he offers a choice between cage and chrysalis and describes a world beyond the one he used to see.
events.action: Alone in the still dark, Trinity says his name, his eyes open, and she reaches for him and kisses him. The image then shows Neo standing alone in a hall, the last Agent gone and the others fled. He leaves the hovercraft's interior for a street phone booth, then rises out of it into the open sky, soaring above the city faster than a speeding bullet with his long black coat billowing behind him. His voice speaks to someone out there in the Matrix, saying they will not have to search for him anymore, that he is done running and done hiding, and leaving whether he is done fighting up to them. He says the Matrix can stay a cage or become a chrysalis, and that to be free you must change yourself rather than the cage. He recalls seeing only edges, boundaries, rules and laws before, but now sees another A realm where everything is possible, a place defined by hope. and peace.

state_triples.reading: This is the one place her guard is allowed to drop—darkness, only the two of them alive—so the tears she usually holds back pour out the instant he answers her. Having spoken love over his body, she now holds living proof that it was heard, and the release is total and private; the scene gives her no audience but Neo, and no words but the kiss.

prose_before_reconcile.action: The two of them are alone in the still dark when Trinity says his name and his eyes open; she reaches for her and she kisses him, and it seems to last forever. The image fades and returns on a computer screen as in the opening, its cursor waiting, until a phone rings, is answered, and a trace program fills the screen. Neo's voice then speaks to someone out there in the Matrix—he knows they are there and can feel them, and imagines they feel him too. He tells them they will not have to search for him anymore, that he is done running and done hiding, leaving whether he is done fighting up to them. He says he believes they both want this world to change, that the Matrix can stay a cage or become a chrysalis, and that to be free you must change yourself rather than the cage. He recalls seeing only edges, boundaries, rules and laws before, but now sees another world where anything can happen, a world full of hope and peace, and that if they free their minds they will find the way.
